rulings.Case Title: IN RE: ANGELITA YANGA ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion For Order Granting Petition For Leave To Present A Late Government Claim
rulings.Rulings: Matter on calendar for Wednesday, July 15, 2026, Line 1, PETITIONER ANGELITA YANGA, ANNABELLA BARQUERA DECEASED, LUCINA ESPIRITU, CIRILA MIRANDA's Motion For Order Granting Petition For Leave To Present A Late Government Claim. Petitioners Angelita Yanga, Lucina Espiritu and Cirila Miranda's motion for order granting petition for leave to present a late government claim is granted, but only in their individual capacities for wrongful death claims for the death of their sister Annabella Barquera, Petitioners' reply memorandum withdraws petitioners' request to present a late government claim in their capacities as successors in interest of Ms. Barquera for survival claims. As to their wrongful death claims, petitioners have shown that they acted with excusable neglect in failing to file government claims within the statutory six month period and respondent City and County of San Francisco has not shown that it would suffer any prejudice if petitioners' late claims were granted. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 302 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. (Dept. 302 Zoom ID 160 409 7690; Passcode 516287.) To appear remotely at the hearing, go to the court's website at sfsuperiorcourt.org under "Online Services," navigate to "Tentative Rulings," and click on the appropriate link, or dial the corresponding phone number. Any party who contests a tentative ruling must send an email to contestdept302tr@sftc.org with a copy to all other parties by 4pm stating, without argument, the portion(s) of the tentative ruling that the party contests. The subject line of the email shall include the line number, case name and case number. The text of the email shall include the name and contact information, including email address, of the attorney or party who will appear at the hearing. Counsel for the prevailing party is required to prepare a proposed order which repeats verbatim the substantive portion of the tentative ruling and must email it to contestdept302tr@sftc.org prior to the hearing even if the tentative ruling is not contested. The court no longer provides a court reporter in the Law & Motion Department. Parties may retain their own reporter, who may appear in the courtroom or remotely. A retained reporter must be a California certified court reporter (CSR), for only a CSR's transcript may be used in California courts. If a CSR is being retained, include in your email all of the following: their name, CSR and telephone numbers, and their individual work email address. =(302/HEK).

rulings.Case Title: FELIPE COLIN VS. MAN-KIT LEUNG M.D. ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: MOTION FOR LEAVE TO Take A Subsequent Deposition Of Andrew Limb, M.D. For Good Cause; Memorandum Of Points And Authorities In Support Thereof
rulings.Rulings: Matter on calendar for Wednesday, July 15, 2026, Line 6, PLAINTIFF FELIPE COLIN's MOTION FOR LEAVE TO Take A Subsequent Deposition Of Andrew Limb, M.D. For Good Cause. Plaintiff Felipe Colin's motion for leave to take a subsequent deposition of Dr. Andrew Limb is granted. Plaintiff has shown good cause for a second deposition of Dr. Limb and nothing in the discovery statutes required that Dr. Limb be served with the motion papers, although it would have both courteous and best practice to do so. The error made by plaintiff's counsel in failing to attend the first deposition of Dr. Limb is regrettable, but not a basis to deprive the plaintiff of deposing a claimed material witness. Plaintiff is limited to three and a half hours for the second deposition and that deposition must take place either by video or at a place selected by Dr. Limb on a date that is agreeable to Dr. Limb no later than August 31, 2026. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 302 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. rulings.Case Title: ALEX EMILIO REYES VS. ALAN C. MAO ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Motion For Order Compelling Plaintiff?S Responses To Defendants Discovery Requests And For An Order Imposing Monetary Sanctions
rulings.Rulings: Matter on calendar for Wednesday, July 15, 2026, Line 9, DEFENDANT ALAN MAO's Motion For Order Compelling Plaintiff's Responses To Defendants Discovery Requests And For An Order Imposing Monetary Sanctions. Defendant Alan Mao's motion for an order compelling responses to Mao's discovery requests and for monetary sanctions is granted. No later than July 31, 2026 plaintiff Alex Reyes must serve verified code-compliant responses without objections to Mao's first sets of form interrogatories, special interrogatories and document requests and produce all responsive documents in his possession, custody and control. Neither Reyes' long period of being out of contact with his counsel nor his lack of employment excuses his failure to timely respond to discovery or is a basis to deny mandatory monetary sanctions where, as here, the discovery failures lacked substantial justification. No later than September 30, 2026 Reyes, but not his counsel, is required to pay Mao the reasonable sanctions of $545 requested by Mao.
